This printing and [[Aurra Sing (AI)]] both use her likeness. |see_also=* [[Michonne Bourriague]] * [[Aurra Sing (AI)]] * [[Alternate Image]] |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Aurra Sing, Tatooine, R |strategy=By I-Ming Chenhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/dark/small/aurrasing.html The mysterious bounty hunter who made a small cameo during [[The Phantom Menace]] will make more than just a mere cameo to the Star Wars: CCG universe. With 4 ability, she is a no-brainer to any Dark Side deck that battles or relies on main characters. Her game text is interesting since it will depend on the opponent losing a character wielding a lightsaber at the same site. Not too common of an event if your opponent is using only Enhanced characters with built-in weapons, but you'll get a good benefit (i.e. higher immunity to attrition) should the opportunity arise. But enough about her game text. There are a variety of different deck types she will go straight into. For players who are big on playing the popular [[Jabba]]'s Palace effect, Scum And Villiany -- using the [[My Kind Of Scum / Fearless And Inventive{{!}}My Kind Of Scum]] objective (JPSD set) or [[Court Of The Vile Gangster / I Shall Enjoy Watching You Die{{!}}Court Of The Vile Gangster]] objective (Enhanced [[Jabba]]'s Palace set) -- Aurra will be a great addition to the rest of the aliens already in your deck. Even if you don't use Scum And Villany, Aurra is still useful in other decks if you like hunting for bounties. In [[Court Of The Vile Gangster / I Shall Enjoy Watching You Die{{!}}Court Of The Vile Gangster]], she gets forfeit +2 and bypasses [[Goo Nee Tay]]. Since Aurra is a bounty hunter, she will qualify for Agents Of The Black Sun (Reflections II/Expanded Universe set), which will benefit from having another bounty hunter. Combos: [[Aurra Sing]] + [[Quietly Observing]]: Why wait until the opponent just lost a character? Have Aurra sneak up on the opponent and just take it. [[Aurra Sing]] + [[Weapon Levitation]]: Arg... just take the lightsaber. I prefer a straight fight to all this sneaking around. [[Aurra Sing]] + [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]: Forget about waiting. Get your own glow stick. Not cheap but you'll be able to add to Force drains and play all the fun interrupts related to lightsabers like [[You Are Beaten]]. |combos=* [[Aurra Sing]] + [[Quietly Observing]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Aurra%20Sing Scomp: Aurra Sing]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). PC-E1 text: “Power +1 on Tatooine. Once per game, during your move phase, may relocate Arica to Luke's location. During your control phase, if present at a battleground (and Luke is not), may retrieve 1 Force. Immune to Undercover and attrition < 4.”Players Committee website card list (VBlock4Type), as captured [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064721/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock4Type.html 2012-07-21] and [https://web.archive.org/web/20130111144021/http://www.starwarsccg.org/cardlists/VBlock4Type.html 2013-01-11] (Internet Archive) The card list drops icons; the icons here are those of the printed slip. Card-list differences are versions (wiki versions ruling, 8 November 2026). The PC website card list was generated from the Players Committee's Holotable card data (research R7, 11 November 2026), so its wording follows that data; it is listed as a version because the PC published it. * '''PC-E2''' ([[Arica (V) (Virtual Block 4) (Errata 2)]]): Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB4-D-arica-pre.gif]]), on the PC website by 25 February 2013 (server upload date)Players Committee card image, file cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual4-Dark/large/arica.gif; the Internet Archive capture of that folder's directory listing ([https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034634/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual4-Dark/large/?C=M;O=A Virtual4-Dark], 18 August 2019) gives every file the date 25-Feb-2013 11:33/11:34 (research R6, 11 November 2026: these are bulk upload dates, and an image may have been made earlier). Today's copy: https://res.starwarsccg.org/cards/legacy/VirtualBlock4-Dark/large/arica.gif: “Power +1 on Tatooine. Once per game, during your move phase, may relocate Arica to Luke's location. During your control phase, if present at a battleground (and Luke is not), may retrieve 1 Force. Immune to Undercover and attrition < 4.” '''What changed:''' the PC card image prints the card-list wording (PC-E1) again, word for word (icons drawn, not written out) except that it spells “Immune” correctly, as the card list does. This unwavering devotion is represented by [[Maul]]'s unique icon, which is neither alien nor Imperial. [[Maul]]'s high deploy cost is comfortably offset by the reduced deploy to [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]], and is reduced even further if he deploys to the [[Tatooine: Hutt Trade Route (Desert){{!}}Desert]] Landing Site. [[Maul]]'s built-in dueling text seems risky with both players drawing the same number of destiny, but adding a duel destiny with a card like [[Focused Attack]] and setting up a high destiny draw with [[Maul's Electrobinoculars]] can quickly swing the duel in the Dark Jedi's favor. Of course, [[Maul]] is incredibly focused thanks to his thirst for revenge against the Jedi. As a result, most characters that aren't Force Attuned are beneath his notice. This is reflected in his gametext that kicks in if none of the Light Side characters at his location have ability of 4 or greater. At such a location, the Light Side's total ability is zero. In other words, the Light Side has no presence at this location, and thus cannot battle or be battled. In addition, it means that the Light Side will need to come up with an ability 4 or higher character in order to block [[Maul]]'s Force drains. Meanwhile, [[Maul]] with his Lightsaber and [[Sniper]] can gradually whittle away the Light Side's characters at his site. Card Size | 63x88mm |} '''Reflections III''' is the 31st Star Wars CCG product, published by Decipher on 31 October 2001. It has 200 cards (100 per side): 100 foils and 100 non-foil premiums. Packs are 18 cards, MSRP $4.95, 30 packs per box. Each pack has '''one foil''' from the list below plus three unique premiums (listed under Card list)[https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists], Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) and random reprints from Premiere through Endor. Those reprints are not listed. A foil of a title that is not on this list is not a Decipher Reflections III pack foil (it may be a [[Promotional Foils|promotional foil]] or a counterfeit).[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]. I like to call him the General Zod of SWCCG. If you plan to base your deck around the Galactic Senate, or if you just want to mop the floor with those weenie Dark Side Senators for laughs, [[Supreme Chancellor Valorum]] is your man. With a hefty 5 Politics, Valorum has the highest concentration of political power in the game. Even better, Valorum has excellent stats outside of the Senate, with 4 Ability (all the better to draw battle destiny when alone at the Senate) and a whopping 7 Forfeit. Top it all off with a multiple-use-friendly 3 Destiny, and the Supreme Chancellor's a shoe-in for any deck. But it's his skill in the Senate that makes Valorum a top choice for any deck. While in a Senate majority, he's a one-man [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]], with the power to cancel an opponent's battle destiny at any site, anywhere, any time, for only 1 Force. That's what I like to call sledgehammer politics. And it's all from the safety of the Galactic Senate, where Walkers and Sith Lords are strictly pooh-poohed. Of course, Valorum's power comes with a price. You remember all those "baseless" accusations we heard about in the movie? Well, they're back with a vengeance. As long as your opponent has Force to spend, he can reduce Valorum's Politics infinitely. While this doesn't hinder Valorum when it comes to guerilla "votes" in the Senate, it does make controlling the Senate with him alone a risky proposition. Be prepared to back him up with other political figures, like [[Queen Amidala]]... or a certain future Supreme Chancellor... Combos: cancel two battle destiny? I'm there! Versions in date order: [[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V)]] (original, release sheet of 11 May 2012); [[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata)]] (PC-E1, PC website card list, by 21 July 2012); '''this page''' (PC-E2, Master List of 27 April 2013, the same words as the original); [[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata 3)]] (PC-E3, Players Committee card image, uploaded 7 May 2013, the same words as the original, the current text). * '''Original''' ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V)]]): text as given in the Virtual Block 8.1 release sheet (official text as of 11 May 2012)[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock8_1.pdf#page=5 Virtual Block 8.1 release sheet] ("Official text as of 11 May 2012"; the surviving copy was re-made 18 July 2012), page 5, slip 30 (position on the sheet; the slip prints no number). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027095418/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock8_1.pdf#page=5 Internet Archive]: “Agenda: order. May be targeted by Might Of The Republic. Your characters with politics (except Wedge and senators) are deploy -1 (and gain [Republic]) here. During your turn, may use 1 Force to ▲ a card with "governor," "political," or "Valorum" in lore.” The Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB8-L-supremechancellorvalorum-pre.gif]]) and the release-sheet slip ([[:File:VB8-03-Supreme_Chancellor_Valorum.png]]) print it. The Master List (official text as of 27 April 2013, Light Side p. 15) prints this text again; under the ruling of 11 November 2026 (every publication is a version), that copy is its own version, PC-E2 (this page); the current text is the PC card image uploaded on 7 May 2013 ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata 3)]], the same words).[[Media:Virtual_Legacy_Final_Master_LS.pdf|Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (Light Side)]], cover "official text as of April 27, 2013" (PDF built February 2014). Original: http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf#page=15, page 15. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170705013057/http://www.starwarsccg.org/Resources/MasterLS.pdf#page=15 Internet Archive] The release-sheet slip prints no slip number. * '''PC-E1''' ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata)]]): The PC website card list (shown there by 21 July 2012, the earliest archived capture with text, and in every capture to 11 January 2013) changed “Agenda:” to “Agendas:”, dropped the parentheses (“deploy -1 and gain [Republic] here”) and moved “Valorum” first (“a card with 'Valorum', 'governor' or 'political' in lore”)Players Committee website card list (VBlock8Type), as captured [https://web.archive.org/web/20120721064747/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/cardlists/VBlock8Type.html 2012-07-21] (Internet Archive); the same text in the captures of 12 December 2012 and 11 January 2013: “Agendas: order. May be targeted by Might Of The Republic. Your characters with politics (except Wedge and senators) are deploy -1 and gain [Republic] here. During your turn, may use 1 Force to ▲ a card with 'Valorum', 'governor' or 'political' in lore.” (The capture of 21 July 2012 prints the ▲ as “/\”; the captures from 12 December 2012 write it out as “take into hand … from Reserve Deck; reshuffle”, which is notation only.) No published card image shows this text; the image of that page is a CardMaker recreation ([[:File:VB8-03-Supreme_Chancellor_Valorum-PC-E1-cardmaker.png]]). The card list was generated from the Players Committee's Holotable card data (research R7, 11 November 2026), so this wording is a transcription the PC published, not a separately announced errata; it is listed because it was published. * '''PC-E2''' (this page): the Players Committee Virtual Cards Master List (official text as of 27 April 2013; Light Side, p. 15) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V)]]) again, word for word: “Agenda: order. May be targeted by Might Of The Republic. Your characters with politics (except Wedge and senators) are deploy -1 (and gain [Republic]) here. During your turn, may use 1 Force to ▲ a card with "governor," "political," or "Valorum" in lore.” It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat of an earlier text); the PC card image uploaded later ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata 3)]]) is the current text. Its image is the Master List slip ([[:File:VL-history-1281-30-front-master.png]]). The Master List slip prints no slip number, like the release-sheet slip and the PC card image. * '''PC-E3''' ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V) (Errata 3)]]): the Players Committee card image ([[:File:VB8-L-supremechancellorvalorum-pre.gif]]) prints the original release-sheet text ([[Supreme Chancellor Valorum (V)]]) again, word for word: “Agenda: order. May be targeted by Might Of The Republic. Your characters with politics (except Wedge and senators) are deploy -1 (and gain [Republic]) here. During your turn, may use 1 Force to ▲ a card with "governor," "political," or "Valorum" in lore.” The image is dated only by its upload to the Players Committee's server: the Apache listing of the Virtual8-Light card-image folder gives every file there the same time, 7 May 2013, 13:52Players Committee server, [https://web.archive.org/web/20190818034752/https://starwarsccg.org/cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Light/large/?C=M;O=A directory listing of cardlists/images/starwars/Virtual8-Light/large/] sorted by date, as captured 18 August 2019 (Internet Archive). That is a bulk upload date, so the image may have been made earlier; it is placed at that date (ruling of 11 November 2026: what was uploaded last counts as the last version). It is listed as a version because it was published (ruling of 11 November 2026: every publication is a version, even a word-for-word repeat). Uploaded after the Master List, it is the latest version and so the current text. Using 4 Force, he's able to send your Jedi from his location to another one while he's sitting on the Council.
